2021 was Hollywood's first full post-lockdown year, and the studios came back swinging with franchise entries, reboots, and a handful of genuine originals. VirtueVigil reviewed and scored all 14 major 2021 theatrical and streaming releases, applying the dual-scoring methodology across every film: Woke Score measures progressive ideological content, Traditional Score measures duty, sacrifice, family loyalty, patriotism, and earned competence.

The results split cleanly along franchise lines. MCU entries range from the franchise's worst ideological offender (Eternals) to its most emotionally devastating traditionally-coded film (Spider-Man: No Way Home). Every film links to the full VirtueVigil review. Ranked from most woke to most traditional.

#1 (Most Woke): Eternals (2021)

WOKE MARGIN: -14 WOKE

Genre: Action / Sci-Fi / Superhero • Platform: Theaters / Disney+

Chloe Zhao's MCU debut assembled the most diverse cast in superhero history and delivered the franchise's first openly gay hero, scoring the highest woke margin of any 2021 film at -14 WOKE. The maximum diversity ensemble is the film's organizing principle rather than its story, and the result earned the MCU's lowest Rotten Tomatoes and IMDB scores on record. The most ideologically ambitious MCU film was also its biggest critical and commercial failure.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Eternals

#2: The Matrix Resurrections (2021)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -6 WOKE

Genre: Sci-Fi Action • Platform: Theaters / HBO Max

Lana Wachowski's self-reflexive sequel makes the trans liberation allegory that was always encoded in the original Matrix mythology fully explicit this time, framing corporate power as the primary villain in a film that simultaneously mocks blockbuster sequel culture while being one. A fascinating failure: it fails as action, partially fails as story, and succeeds as a piece of cinema that forces genuine engagement with its own contradictions.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of The Matrix Resurrections

#3: Red Notice (2021)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -6 WOKE

Genre: Action / Comedy / Heist • Platform: Netflix

Netflix's $200 million heist comedy works on the surface until the ending, which exists specifically to reveal that Gal Gadot's villain was the mastermind who outmaneuvered every male lead from the start. Law enforcement is portrayed as globally incompetent bureaucracy throughout. Fun when it stays in motion, undermined by the structural female supremacy framing baked into its third-act twist.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Red Notice

#4: Black Widow (2021)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: -5 WOKE

Genre: Action / Adventure / Thriller • Platform: Theaters / Disney+

Natasha Romanoff's belated solo film frames the Red Room program explicitly as a #MeToo allegory about institutionalized control over women's bodies, including forced sterilization as a plot point. Florence Pugh's Yelena is the film's genuine highlight, and the dysfunctional-family dynamic provides real entertainment, but the feminist revenge framework driving the central conflict holds the score in negative territory.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Black Widow

#5: Cruella (2021)

MIXED MARGIN: -2 WOKE

Genre: Crime / Comedy-Drama • Platform: Theaters / Disney+

Disney ran Cruella de Vil through the villain rehabilitation machine, producing a girlboss origin story that justifies the iconic villain's cruelty through backstory trauma. The Joker-meets-The-Devil-Wears-Prada approach delivers genuine style and Emma Stone in peak form, but the underlying framework, that evil is always explained by victimhood, earns the slight negative margin.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Cruella

#6: No Time to Die (2021)

MIXED MARGIN: +0 TRAD

Genre: Action / Spy Thriller • Platform: Theaters

Daniel Craig's farewell is a film at war with itself. A Black female 007 replacement and a domesticated, emotionally vulnerable Bond push the score left; Bond's ultimate self-sacrifice for his family and his final commitment to duty over survival push it right. The elements cancel out in a film that earns its ending but fights itself across 163 minutes to get there. Craig's finest acting, the franchise's most divided legacy.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of No Time to Die

#7: Space Jam: A New Legacy (2021)

TRADITIONAL LEAN MARGIN: +4 TRAD

Genre: Live Action / Animated Sports Comedy • Platform: Theaters / HBO Max

LeBron James and the Looney Tunes fight a Warner Bros. algorithm in a film that is itself a Warner Bros. algorithm. Lola Bunny's desexualization and the diverse ensemble framing register, but the father-son bond between LeBron and his estranged son Dom is the film's genuine emotional engine, nudging the overall score into positive territory despite the cynical IP exercise surrounding it.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Space Jam: A New Legacy

#8: Mortal Kombat (2021)

TRADITIONAL LEAN MARGIN: +4 TRAD

Genre: Martial Arts Action Fantasy • Platform: Theaters / HBO Max

The 2021 reboot delivers faithful fatalities, a Scorpion-Sub-Zero feud built on genuine honor and cross-generational vengeance, and enough martial arts discipline to register as traditionally coded. The insertion of original character Cole Young, a non-white protagonist who exists to replace white roster members, and the default diverse ensemble hold it back from higher ground, but the film earns its +4 TRAD by actually caring about the source material's warrior code.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Mortal Kombat

#9: Free Guy (2021)

TRADITIONAL LEAN MARGIN: +8 TRAD

Genre: Action Comedy Sci-Fi • Platform: Theaters / Disney+

Ryan Reynolds plays an NPC who chooses to become a hero through genuine virtue rather than birth or circumstance, and it works better than it has any right to. The competent female lead runs the support structure, and corporate villainy is the antagonist, but the film's central message, that choosing good is meaningful even inside a system designed against it, lands as a surprisingly earnest traditional framework about individual agency and moral choice.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Free Guy

#10: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings (2021)

TRADITIONAL LEAN MARGIN: +9 TRAD

Genre: Action / Adventure / Fantasy • Platform: Theaters / Disney+

Marvel's first Asian-led film delivered a deeply traditional family drama disguised as a representation exercise. Filial loyalty, the weight of inherited responsibility, and the tension between a son's identity and his father's legacy drive the story's real emotional core. The Chinese cultural specificity is handled with reverence rather than stereotyping, and the father-son-daughter family conflict grounds the superhero spectacle in something genuine.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Shang-Chi

#11: Encanto (2021)

TRADITIONAL LEAN MARGIN: +10 TRAD

Genre: Animation / Musical / Fantasy • Platform: Theaters / Disney+

Disney's Colombian magical-family story earns its emotional payoff by centering family obligation, generational sacrifice, and the cost of perfectionism on the family unit. Body positivity messaging and anti-perfectionism framing register, but the film's resolution places the family's roots and collective bonds above individual gifts and personal ambition, landing it firmly in traditional territory as a rare modern animated film that respects the family structure it depicts.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Encanto

#12: Dune: Part One (2021)

TRADITIONAL MARGIN: +13 TRAD

Genre: Sci-Fi Epic • Platform: Theaters / HBO Max

Denis Villeneuve's long-fought adaptation honors duty, sacrifice, and the weight of leadership while delivering Frank Herbert's explicit warning against messianic politics. Duke Leto's honor and self-sacrifice, the Fremen's cultural rootedness, and the film's anti-messianic framework carry the score. The Bene Gesserit all-female power structure and diverse casting beyond the source material hold it below the top tier, but this is serious filmmaking that respects its audience.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Dune: Part One

#13: Ghostbusters: Afterlife (2021)

TRADITIONAL MARGIN: +15 TRAD

Genre: Supernatural Adventure Comedy • Platform: Theaters / Paramount+

The most traditionally conservative blockbuster of 2021. A sincere, emotionally honest film about family legacy, the courage of children to honor their ancestors, and the importance of standing against genuine evil. The Spengler grandchildren carry their grandfather's work forward through inherited competence and earned love rather than birthright entitlement. The female lead and single-mother default family structure hold it back from STRONGLY TRADITIONAL, but Ghostbusters: Afterlife is a genuine conservative crowd-pleaser.

Read the full VirtueVigil review of Ghostbusters: Afterlife

#14 (Most Traditional): Spider-Man: No Way Home (2021)

TRADITIONAL MARGIN: +19 TRAD

Genre: Superhero / Action / Science Fiction • Platform: Theaters / Netflix

One of the most emotionally devastating blockbusters of the decade. Peter Parker earns the highest traditional score of any 2021 film through the ultimate sacrifice: he chooses to let everyone who loves him forget he exists in order to save the world. Responsibility, self-sacrifice, and the full cost of heroism drive a score that would be higher still without the race-swapped core characters and multiverse framing. The ending hits hard precisely because the film earned it frame by frame.

Methodology

All scores use the VirtueVigil dual-scoring system. Woke Score measures the density and intensity of progressive ideological content across categories including gender politics, religious critique, racial messaging, sexual content framing, and institutional critique. Traditional Score measures duty, sacrifice, family loyalty, moral clarity, patriotism, and earned competence. The Score Margin is the difference between the two, with positive numbers indicating a traditional lean and negative numbers indicating a woke lean. For complete methodology details, see the VirtueVigil Methodology page.
